data.title: Akt promotes cell survival by phosphorylating and inhibiting a Forkhead transcription factor
data.authors: Brunet A; Blenis J et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Mammalian cell lines; primary neurons (in vitro)
data.finding: Akt phosphorylates the Forkhead transcription factor FKHRL1 (a FOXO family member), driving its cytoplasmic retention via 14-3-3 binding and blocking Fas-ligand-driven apoptosis — the discovery that placed FOXO transcription factors downstream of Akt/PI3K survival signalling.
data.abstract_excerpt: Survival factors can suppress apoptosis in a transcription-independent manner by activating the serine/threonine kinase Akt, which then phosphorylates and inactivates components of the apoptotic machinery, including BAD and Caspase 9. In this study, we demonstrate that Akt also regulates the activity of FKHRL1, a member of the Forkhead family of transcription factors. In the presence of survival factors, Akt phosphorylates FKHRL1, leading to FKHRL1's association with 14-3-3 proteins and FKHRL1's retention in the cytoplasm.

extracted_findings.species: Mammalian cell lines; primary neurons (in vitro)
extracted_findings.effect: Akt phosphorylates FKHRL1 (FOXO), blocking its nuclear translocation and Fas-ligand-driven apoptosis upon survival-factor withdrawal
